column4: FPL-GTR-282 chapter 5: Table 5-3a bending MOE 7700 MPa times 1.10 gives E_L = 8470 MPa; Table 5-1 ratios E_R/E_L 0.081, G_LR/E_L 0.087, G_LT/E_L 0.086, G_RT/E_L 0.005; Table 5-2 nu_LR 0.378; Table 5-3a SG 0.32 gives density = 1000 x 0.32 x 1.12 = 358.4 kg/m3. Absolute values are those ratios times E_L
column5: The plan names cedar for the back bars and the neck without a species; Spanish cedar (Cedrela odorata) is the usual guitar cedar and is not in the Wood Handbook's elastic tables, so western redcedar is a SURROGATE of lower density. Axis convention: material axis 1 = L (grain), axis 2 = R (across the growth rings, in the plane of a quartersawn plate), thickness = T, so shear_modulus_12 = G_LR, shear_modulus_13 = G_LT and shear_modulus_23 = G_RT, poisson_ratio_12 = nu_LR (strain along R per strain along L under stress along L). Moduli are static or quasi-static handbook values at about 12 percent moisture content, used here at audio frequency; the validity band omega 0 to 2 pi 2000 rad/s and T 280 to 320 K is the band in which this use is DECLARED by the pack author, not a measured band (wood storage moduli typically rise a few percent per decade of frequency). Loss: five dimensionless loss factors loss_factor_1 (L), loss_factor_2 (R), loss_factor_12 (L-R shear), loss_factor_13 (L-T shear) and loss_factor_23 (R-T shear) in the material axes, valid for 2 pi 50 to 2 pi 1000 rad/s (a band declared by the pack author, not measured), for the constant-loss-factor shell path; and the nine Kelvin-Voigt viscosities built from the same loss factors as eta x stiffness / omega_ref with omega_ref = 2 pi 200 rad/s (1256.64 rad/s): plane_stress_viscosity_11, _22, _66 and the through-thickness shears are eta_L, eta_R, eta_LR, eta_LT, eta_RT times the corresponding stiffness over omega_ref, the Poisson cross term _12 uses the ARITHMETIC mean of eta_L and eta_R times Q12 / omega_ref (the Adams-Bacon split of the stiffness by loss channel, so both realisations agree on every entry), and the 16 and 26 entries are zero by the orthotropic axes. Wood's loss factor is nearly constant, so the pack states omega_ref as constant_loss_reference_omega, and the shell reduction applies each loss factor at every mode's own frequency; read as Kelvin-Voigt, the same viscosities would make the loss factor proportional to frequency. The loss factors are measured on other specimens and are NOT a measurement of the Esteso guitar.
